overall: The AG found the School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating over email (Chair's Oct. 15, 2012 email and a member's reply), but not by the Chair's Oct. 18 email to the search consultant.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair emailed members a document developed in open session and asked for their input, which the complainant said was improper email deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: The Chair's October 15, 2012 email constituted improper deliberation because it was sent to a quorum of the Committee and solicited Committee members' opinions outside of a meeting.

allegations.summary: A committee member replied by email attaching suggested edits to the document, which the complaint treated as part of the email deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: The response sent by one of the Committee members, attaching suggested edits to a document, was also deliberation.

allegations.summary: The Chair's follow-up email after the complaint asked for last suggestions to be sent to the search consultant, challenged as further deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: The Chair's October 18, 2012 email was not deliberation, however, because it provided a document to be discussed at a meeting, and requested that suggested edits be sent to a non-Committee member for review, in this case the Superintendent Search Consultant.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; the complaint is considered resolved, relying on the Committee's vote that future input go directly to third-party consultants.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with Open Meeting Law, and consider the complaint addressed by this determination to be resolved.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
